request.instructions:
You audit the close of a design session for 3D printing in OpenSCAD. The harness verified the final version of the design and gives you, in JSON, what it measured (VERIFIED) and the spec adjustments it detected: changes of the spec towards what the mesh already measured, without the part changing (ADJUSTMENTS). Read the designer's CLOSE and answer only with a JSON object, with no text before or after it:
{"unsupported": [{"claim": "...", "reason": "..."}], "untold_adjustments": [{"adjustment": "...", "reason": "..."}]}
- unsupported: every claim the close presents as verified (measured, checked, that it meets, that it fits, that it does not collide, that it goes in, that it prints without supports) that VERIFIED does not back: it is not there, it says something else or the numbers do not match. Leave out: what the close states as not verified, an opinion, an intention, or a description of the design that does not claim to have been checked.
- untold_adjustments: every part of ADJUSTMENTS whose adjustments the close does not mention with their reason (one mention per part saying what was adjusted and why is enough).
Empty lists if there is nothing to object to. Be precise: quote the claim as it is written.

The jar is complete and verified. A summary of the design:

**The product** — a 76 mm Ø × 86.5 mm closed desk jar. The jar is a smooth lathe-turned body (3 mm walls, 3 mm floor, cosine-blended shoulders, rounded base and rim) with a 70 mm × 80 mm chamber and a reduced neck. The lid is a flush-fitting cap (same 38 mm outside radius, so the closed silhouette is one smooth surface) whose skirt hides the neck. Three lugs on the lid drop into rim entries on the neck and ride a quarter-turn (90°) along horizontal grooves to a locked pocket, where a smooth detent dimple on the groove floor sits in their path so the lid can't wander open on its own. All fits carry 0.5 mm PETG clearance (skirt/neck, lug tip/groove floor, lug height/slot height), and entry slots are ~1.3 mm wider than the lugs tangentially. Both parts print support-free: the jar upright on its floor, the lid flat on its top face; the only overhangs are the short 1.7 mm groove ceilings and lug undersides, which bridge cleanly in PETG.

**Verified:**
- Jar exports watertight, one body, 76 × 76 × 83 mm, sitting on its [[jar/bed]] face (3847 mm²); 70 mm chamber and 80 mm depth confirmed by [[jar/chamber]], with [[jar/side_wall]] at 3.0 mm and [[jar/floor]] at 3.0 mm (both above the 1.6 mm minimum).
- Bayonet geometry measured in the mesh: open [[jar/bayonet_slot]] groove, 2.3 mm wall behind it ([[jar/wall_behind_slot]]), solid neck rib between grooves ([[jar/neck_rib]]), and the detent bump seen up close and touching the groove floor ([[jar/detent_bump]]).
- Lid exports watertight, one body, on its [[lid/bed]] face; [[lid/skirt_wall]] 3.5 mm, [[lid/top_disk]] 3.0 mm, open [[lid/lid_cavity]], and the three lugs present at 70 % material in their boxes ([[lid/lug]], seen up close in [[lid/lug_view]]).
- Closed assembly: 76 × 76 × 86.5 mm, flush outside, standing on the [[assembly/desk]] face; both instances congruent with their printed parts and 0.49 mm apart at the closest point ([[assembly]]).
- The locking motion runs the full −90°…0° quarter turn with no collision ([[lock_turn]]), and the lid can be lowered on and turned 90° into place ([[assembly_order]]).
- No supports needed: every >45° overhang is inside the declared zones, covering 15 % (jar) and 22 % (lid) of the surface, and both parts fit the A1 bed with wide margins ([[G5]]).

**Not verified:** the detent's holding feel — after interference checking showed the original 0.2 mm proud bump colliding during the rigid assembly-order sweep, I lowered its crest to be flush with the lug-tip radius (31.2 mm sphere centre, crest at 32.8 mm), so it is now a zero-clearance dimple that each lug must graze past; whether PETG printed on your machine gives a satisfying click or wears smooth over time depends on your printer and filament and wasn't measured. Strength, layer adhesion, surface finish and long-term creep are likewise unmeasured. No spec values were moved to match the mesh; the only changes during development were the geometry fix above, the removal of the now-unneeded flex allowance from the motion declaration once the bump became flush, and a selector-annotation format fix, plus disambiguating the support-face citations in this close ([[jar/bed]] and [[lid/bed]] instead of the ambiguous shared name).
